title: Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) engages with National Highways Authority of India to strengthen implementation of Labour Codes and enhance stakeholder consultation
body_text: The Office of the Chief Labour Commissioner (Central), Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India, convened a meeting with senior officers of the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) on 27 th November 2026 under the chairpersonship of Ms. Sonal Mishra, IAS, Chief Labour Commissioner (Central), at Shramev Jayate Bhawan, Dwarka, New Delhi, to discuss effective implementation of the Labour Codes, 2020 and strengthen coordination and stakeholder consultation. The meeting was organised as part of the series of one-to-one interactions being undertaken by the Office of the Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) [CLC(C)] with various Ministries, Departments and Central Public Sector Undertakings to facilitate effective implementation of the Labour Codes, promote compliance and strengthen institutional coordination. The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) was represented by Shri C. K. Sinha, CGM, Admin, alongside their team. All Senior officers from the Office of the CLC(C)] attended the meeting. During the meeting, the Office of the CLC(C) made a presentation covering the overview of the Labour Codes and key provisions relevant to the National Highways Authority of India, essential labour compliance requirements, issues relating to contract labour, registration and licensing requirements, and the use of digital platforms. The role of the CLC(C) organisation in facilitating compliance and ensuring ease of doing business was also highlighted. The meeting focused on several key issues, including conducting an on-the-spot registration and licensing drive for contractors and sub-contractors to facilitate statutory compliance under the Labour Codes. Emphasis was also laid on immediate reporting of accidents in accordance with Section 10 of the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020. NHAI was requested to share its accident-related Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and best practices, including measures undertaken for conducting mock drills and ensuring workplace safety. It was, further, deliberated that a Joint Working Group comprising representatives from 2–4 NHAI Regional Offices and the Office of the CLC(C) may be constituted to examine and facilitate issues relating to statutory benefits for women workers and inter-State migrant workers engaged at linear project sites. The representatives of NHAI appreciated this initiative of CLC Organisation as a key facilitation measures and assured for all cooperation in effective implementation of Labour Codes. The Office of CLC(C) is undertaking such structured interactions with concerned Ministries, Departments and organisations to promote awareness, facilitate compliance, strengthen digital enablement and ensure smooth and effective implementation of the four Labour Codes. ***** Rini Choudhury / Aishwarya Asthana
